claim: Hezari and Zelditch prove that an ellipse of sufficiently small eccentricity is spectrally unique up to isometry among all smooth planar domains, with no symmetry, convexity, or closeness-to-ellipse assumption on the comparison class.
stance_target: existence of near-degeneracy / near-diagonal recovery results as a methodological cousin to a planned stability theorem
scope_conditions: planar smooth domains, Dirichlet Laplacian, small-eccentricity regime
quoted_support: We show that if the eccentricity of an ellipse is sufficiently small then up to isometries it is spectrally unique among all smooth domains. We do not assume any symmetry, convexity, or closeness to the ellipse, on the class of domains.

claim: Hezari-Zelditch's result, though set in a near-degenerate regime (small eccentricity, i.e. near-circular), is an exact rigidity/determinacy statement valid below an implicit eccentricity threshold, not a quantitative bound on how spectral distance controls shape distance as the threshold is approached.
stance_target: near-degeneracy inverse spectral results in the literature are typically rigidity/determinacy statements, not stability estimates that quantify blow-up as a degenerate configuration is approached
scope_conditions: as stated in the arXiv abstract, arXiv:1907.03882v2
quoted_support: We show that if the eccentricity of an ellipse is sufficiently small then up to isometries it is spectrally unique among all smooth domains.
